title: Kotlin Null Safety for Android Interviews

scenes.line1: Ever crashed an app with null?
scenes.say: Have you ever crashed an app because of a null reference? Let’s see how Kotlin helps you avoid that.

scenes.label: Types
scenes.sub: Kotlin distinguishes between nullable and non-nullable types.
scenes.say: Kotlin’s type system separates types that can be null from those that can’t. This is a big step in preventing runtime errors.

scenes.code:
val name: String? = getName()
val length = name?.length ?: 0
scenes.say: Here’s how you safely access a property. If name is null, length becomes zero instead of crashing your app.
First, add a question mark to make a type nullable. Next, use the safe call operator to access properties. Finally, use the Elvis operator to set a default value if it’s null.

scenes.question: Can you ignore null safety in Kotlin?
scenes.right: No, Kotlin enforces null safety at compile time to prevent crashes.
scenes.say: Don’t fall for this trap. Kotlin’s null safety isn’t optional—it’s built into the language to catch errors before your code runs.
